title: Refusals name their spot: adopt GenError::invalid_at at the remaining located refusal sites (#261 follow-up)
body:
Follow-up to #261 part 2 (PR forthcoming from `vilts:issue/261-refused-location`).

**Today (with that PR):** a generator refusal can name the spot it is about (`GenError::invalid_at(msg, spot)` → `CommandError::MachiningAt`). The viewport marks that spot and the op page's refusal line frames it. Only the first adopters do so: Face's narrow strip between two holes, the drill cycle's R-plane / counterbore / bore-fit / centre-cutting doors, Bore's and Thread's counterbore and fit doors, and the plunge law. The other roughly 620 `GenError::Invalid` / `Empty` sites name no spot. Their refusal shows text only, as before.

**Expected:** every refusal that is about one place on the part names it. Candidates found by a grep for coordinates in the refusal text:
- app: `operation/cross_part.rs`, `cross_stock.rs`, `drill_reach.rs` (2 sites), `drill_top.rs`, `rotary_gate.rs` (2), `stitch_cross.rs`
- motion: `drilling/axial.rs` (4), `drilling/cross.rs` (3), `finishing3d/deburr.rs`, `multiaxis/rotary_links.rs`, `turning/bore/mod.rs`, `turning/contour/rides.rs`, `turning/thread.rs`

There may be more whose sentence names a feature rather than a coordinate.

**How:** swap `GenError::Invalid(format!(..))` for `GenError::invalid_at(format!(..), spot)`. The spot must be in the frame the generator runs in, because `run_job` maps it to world. A turning kernel's spot is in its meridian frame, and that frame needs its own mapping first. Any code or test that matches `GenError::Invalid(_)` on an adopted site must also accept `GenError::At { .. }`.

**Done means:** each listed site either names its spot, with a test asserting the world spot, or carries a one-line comment on why it names none (for example a turning meridian with no world mapping yet).

Suggested labels: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `area:2d`, `source:agent` (filed by an agent for an outside contributor, who cannot set labels).

Part of #261.
